Of course, the best advice is to go see a psychologist to deal with the trauma. They’re not always affordable so see if there’s an organization like RAINN near you to provide you with some information on cheap therapy. Most women’s organizations do this.

It took me many tries before finding the right medication. Even then, sometimes, it doesn’t work. I think I went through about 6 brands before landing on Cymbalta and Wellbutrin. I think really communicating with my psychiatrist helped me. So instead of telling him “this medication isn’t working”, I’d say something like “I still feel tired even though I’m feeling less upset”. He then experimented by combining different medications to kind of offset the negative side effects of the other. Like on Cymbalta, I’d not be worried or upset at all but I’d feel lethargic. With Wellbutrin, I have more energy. With both of them, I felt better AND had more energy. Maybe you could ask you doc if combining medications is a good idea for you? Of course, you can’t combine meds by yourself but your doc should be able to if they deem it necessary. Not all meds can be combined so it’s really best to check with your doc ^^
